value: Cycle the UNESCO-listed vineyards of Champagne in luxury on a self-guided cycling holiday from Épernay, where sun-drenched slopes, Grand Cru villages and centuries of sparkling tradition await you at every turn of the pedal.

Settle into La Villa Eugène, the beautifully restored 19th-century home of the Mercier family, set in a lush private park on the prestigious Avenue de Champagne. From here, stroll past grand mansion façades that rise above miles of underground galleries, where millions of bottles rest in cool darkness. Ride out through the rolling Marne Valley to Hautvillers, the village where the Benedictine monk Dom Pérignon is said to have discovered sparkling wine and where he now rests in the abbey, learning the secrets of Blanc de Noirs as you pass Fleury-la-Rivière and Oeuilly. Next, follow the Marne River to Aÿ, with its Gothic church and timber-framed houses, then continue to Montebello castle in Mareuil-sur-Aÿ and the old church of Condé-sur-Marne, surrounded by fruity Pinot Meunier vines. On your final ride, glide along the chalky slopes of the Côte des Blancs, home of elegant Chardonnay and Blanc de Blancs, through the Grand Cru villages of Avize, Cramant and Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, tucked between vineyard and forest.

This package includes 4 nights' 5-star accommodation at a single hotel, all breakfasts, bike hire (a Giant Argento RS4 or equivalent with rear pannier and phone holder), a bike fitting and briefing, and a navigation app to guide your way. Daily loops of 43–47 km follow quiet country lanes, cycle paths and vineyard tracks with some steady climbs, best suited to regular cyclists, and an e-bike upgrade offers a gentler pace. Because the holiday is self-guided, you set the rhythm, whether that means lingering over a long lunch or adding the optional visit package, with champagne house tastings in Hautvillers, at Moët & Chandon in Épernay and at Château de Boursault.
Raise a glass to golden vineyards, chalk-cut cellars and the quiet luxury of Épernay, and come discover Champagne one sparkling village at a time.
Moderate to Challenging

value: Arrive in Epernay, a town entirely surrounded by vines that competes for the title of 'Capital of Champagne'.
Walk down the Avenue de Champagne, with mansion facades and homes occupied by famous Champagne Houses.
Epernay has miles of underground galleries storing millions of bottles of champagne.
Cellar visits to the largest Champagne houses are mentioned; these are available through the optional Visit package and are not included.
Overnight at La Villa Eugene.
Loop ride from Epernay themed on 'Blanc de Noirs' champagne, made only from black grapes (Pinot Noir and/or Pinot Meunier).
Cycle routes bordered with vineyards, with views over the undulating Marne Valley, to Hautvillers.
Hautvillers is where Benedictine monk Dom Perignon is said to have accidentally invented effervescent wine at the end of the 17th century; he is buried in the abbey of Hautvillers.
Continue through wine villages such as Fleury la Riviere and Oeuilly.
The optional Visit package includes a champagne house visit and tasting in Hautvillers (not included).
Breakfast
Loop ride themed on Pinot Meunier, grown in the Marne Valley, which gives rosé champagnes their fruity flavour.
The route follows the Marne River to Ay, with a high Gothic-style church and wood-frame houses, including one reputed to have served as Henri IV's fermenting room.
Continue to Conde sur Marne (Roman church of Conde) and pass the Montebello castle in Mareuil sur Ay, with panoramic views.
Breakfast

value.season: Headwater's France holidays run from mid-May to the end of September or early October (France-wide statement).
value.conditions: Weather is described as suitable for cycling in France for the whole period. To avoid summer heat, May/early June and after mid-September are recommended (statement mentions the Loire and Brittany).
value.packingNote: Even in summer, France can see its fair share of rain; a light waterproof is advised.
